text: She did get it eventually.
In 1876, Queen Victoria was proclaimed Empress of India.
Under the Raj, India got railways, telegraph lines, universities and a new class of English
educated Indians.
The first passenger train ran in 1853 from Bombay to Thane.
Remember the railway that buried the bricks of Harappa?
Same era. Full circle.
Kind of.
But the railways were built mainly to carry raw cotton to the ports
and British factory cloth back in.
India, once the world's great cloth maker,
now bought its cloth from Manchester.
And famines kept coming.
In the great famine of 1876, millions died, while grain was still being exported.
An Indian thinker named Dadabai Naoroji added up the numbers and gave it a name, the Drain
of wealth. Money flowing out of India year after year.
Remember that quarter of the world's economy? By 1950 India's share had fallen
to about 4%. The shop wasn't just unlocked, it was emptied. But the same
Some schools and newspapers the British built gave Indians the tools to fight back.
Not with swords this time, with ideas.
